 The number one trending GitHub repo this week is called Reverse Engineer Anything. You point your coding agent at an app and it shows you how that app works. You're not stealing source code or anything, but say you love a particular app feature. This shows you exactly how it's built so you can build your own. This can also bring old hardware back to life. One person got their Logitech keypad running on Linux in 15 minutes. Other people are trying it on scanners and old sound cards that lost driver support. 70,000 stars so far. It's absolutely free, runs on your own machine, and works on cloud code and codecs, comment decode, and I'll send you the link.
